scope: Measure output and constructor offsets, nested and vector records, frame offsets and display, R_ epoch labels, position vectors and direction consumers.

comparison.result: 140 recorded reference and frame cases pass. All 101 release timings are faster than CASA, from 1.20x to 32.75x.
comparison.controls: Nine measure types, same and cross references, input and output origins, nested and vector offsets, malformed and mismatched offsets, apparent and modeled directions, epoch rounding, and raw display strings. Review regressions cover same-model origins in spectral projections, frame insertion refusing origins that would need the tool's ambient frame, and near-geocentre WGS84 convergence. Known CASA constructor and field-norm defects use the independent geometry controls.
comparison.tolerances: Exact keys, canonical reference codes, units, shapes and text. Numeric comparisons use 2e-11 relative and 2e-7 absolute, with Cartesian controls for the known magnetic deviations.

performance.conditions: Same bundled data and CASA Python process. One warm-up and seven retained samples of 400 calls for each successful case.

validation: 2044 affected Python cases and 311 Rust unit cases. The three tool-signature checks also pass in CASA's Python environment. Formatting, scoped Clippy, strict rustdoc, architecture and docs checks.
review: One local Astra xhigh review. Repaired three independently reproduced defects and verified eight recorded cases that fail before and pass after, covering active planetary spectral projections, frame insertion, and near-geocentre WGS84 convergence.
